limitation_addressed: G1: small effect |delta|<=0.05 requires larger sample
approach: Inverse power analysis: Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE) at the CURRENT pooled sample (n=1193, per-group n_per=596.5), two-proportion z-test, alpha=0.05 two-sided, equal per-group n.  Replaces the 'needs larger sample' statement with an exact detection-limit number.
conclusion: With the current n=1193 (n_per=596.5), the smallest effect the study can detect is |delta| = 0.0740 (80% power) / 0.0850 (90% power), corresponding to Cohen's h = 0.162 / 0.188.  The OBSERVED effect (|delta|=0.1425, h=0.327) is 1.9x above the 80% detection limit and 1.7x above the 90% limit.  Hence the '|delta|<=0.05 needs a larger sample' limitation is not binding here: the study is NOT under-powered for the effect it actually reports; it would only be under-powered for effects below the MDE (a |delta| of 0.0740 or smaller), which is a detection-limit boundary, not a failure to detect the reported effect.
